name: Why? we only buy full-grain leather — and how to tell the difference
description: There are four grades of leather sold to upholstery shops. Three of them shouldn't be in your living room. Here's how to read a hide before it ends up on a chair you'll regret in eighteen months.
author: Mark Lockhart
textSecondary: Full-grain leather is the only grade that develops a patina over time. Everything else either peels, cracks or fades. We break down the differences so you can make an informed decision before you sign.

name: Eight-way hand-tied: what it is and why it costs what it costs
description: The seat construction every upholsterer says they offer and few actually do. We break down the steps that make the price.
author: Dave Reinhart
textSecondary: Hand-tied springs require more time, more skill and more materials than any other seat construction method. We explain exactly why — and what you're missing without it.

name: When to restore, when to walk away: a frame-by-frame guide
description: Not every old chair is worth saving. Here's what we look at first when a piece arrives for an assessment.
author: Jamie Costa
textSecondary: We've turned away jobs that other shops would have taken. Here's the checklist we use when a piece comes in for evaluation — and the honest criteria for when restoration makes financial sense.

name: Oak, ash, walnut: choosing the right hardwood for a custom build
description: The three woods we use ninety percent of the time, and what each one does that the others don't.
author: Mark Lockhart
textSecondary: Wood selection determines how the piece ages, how it machines, and how much it costs. We explain our choices in plain terms.

name: A tour of the bench: what each station does
description: Eight people, five rooms, one rule — every piece touches every station. Here's how it flows.
author: Dave Reinhart
textSecondary: From the lumber rack to the finishing room, a Red Eight piece passes through five distinct stations. Here's what happens at each one.

name: From sketch to seat: how the Reading-room chair came together
description: Six rounds of drawings, two prototypes, one chair the library couldn't stop ordering. The process behind a quiet piece.
author: Lena Park
textSecondary: Designing a chair that invites people to stay for three hours requires more than ergonomics. Here's the design process behind one of our best-selling pieces.
